s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital swelling with vision deterioration and proptosis
salient_findings: Left fronto-orbital swelling of 10 years’ duration
Progressive deterioration of vision in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis with inferior and medial displacement of the left globe
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Left fronto-orbital swelling for 10 years
Progressive vision deterioration in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis with displacement of the left globe
No history of endocrine abnormalities
Contrast-enhanced MRI shows heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof
Axial CT scan shows expansive lytic bony lesion in the orbit
Lesion involves the superior and lateral walls of the orbit, including the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Long-standing orbital swelling and lytic bony lesion with heterogeneous enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the sphenoid wing and dural-based lesion

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bony destruction and mass effect

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion with possible soft tissue component

shortlist.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital roof involvement and mixed lytic/sclerotic appearance

raw.rationale: The long duration of symptoms (10 years) and the presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass with an expansive lytic bony lesion are consistent with fibrous dysplasia, which is a benign but potentially debilitating condition that can cause progressive bone lesions and displacement of surrounding structures.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: While meningioma could explain some of the imaging findings, it typically presents with more rapid onset of symptoms and is less likely to cause the long-standing bone changes seen in this case.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Osteosarcoma is an aggressive malignancy that would likely cause more rapid progression of symptoms and significant pain, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumor is typically seen in older patients and is less likely to cause the long-standing bone changes and gradual vision deterioration seen in this case.

rejected.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
rejected.why: Fibro-osseous lesion is a broad term that could encompass fibrous dysplasia, but it is less specific and does not provide a clear explanation for the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.
